label: SIMULATED. Hypothetical backtests on past data. Not investment advice, not a recommendation, no trades are placed. Past results do not predict future results.

assumptions.filing_delay: copy runs enter after the filing date

caveats.text: Amounts are disclosed ranges, not exact. Size buckets use the low end of the range. Dollar-weighted results are not computed.
Costs are assumptions, not measurements. No taxes, no market impact, execution at the close.
Only derived aggregates are published, never raw filings or price series. Source terms apply.
Filings arrive up to 45 days after the trade, sometimes later. Rows with a missing or impossible filing date are dropped and counted. Entering on the trade date is not achievable for the public.
Rows without a usable ticker (bonds, funds without symbols, private assets, options) are excluded and counted. Ticker renames and reuse can cause mismatches.
A statistical pattern in disclosed trades does not show use of nonpublic information.
The data does not show whether a trade was the member's, a spouse's or a dependent's.
Prices use adjusted close when available, otherwise close (price return only, no dividends).
About five years of data and one market regime. There are few independent windows at 180 days.
The price universe is the tickers Congress traded plus a fixed ETF set. Delisted or acquired names may be missing or cut short, which flatters stock-picking results.
Congress trades large, popular US names. Doing better than SPY can reflect that tilt, so results are also compared with random picks from the same universe.
